result.markdown: # Variable names ![](/images/nametag.png){style="width:250px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"} R conventions are style guides. You do not need to follow them but they are intended to help make code easier to read. There are lots of different suggestions for different parts of R code. In this page we will look at conventions for __variable names__. ## Rules ![](/images/rules.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"} __Variable names__ have certain rules that must be followed. We covered these in the [variable assignment page](/foundations/variables.qmd) but below is a reminder: - Must start with a letter - Cannot contain spaces - Cannot start with a number - Cannot share the same name as a command or function in R - They are case sensitive - The __variable__ name `BB` is different to the __variable__ name `bb` which is different again to `bB` ## Naming styles On top of these rules there are a few naming styles that are recommended. It is very good to choose one naming style and stick with it (unless you have a reason not to). Below are three commonly used naming conventions for R. Look through them and choose your favourite to use. ::: {.callout-important} Don't run any of the code in this page. Trying to run variable names that don't exist will produce errors in R. ::: ### Snake case ![](/images/snake_case.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} Snake case is my preferred naming convention and the one used in these materials. It consists of using lower case letters with underscores (`_`) between words. Numbers can also be used. Below are some examples of names in snake case. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} one two_df two_2_df three_four_five three_four_five_2_vec this_is_snake_case ``` ::: ### Period separated ![](/images/period_separated.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} Period separated is almost identical to snake case. All you need to do is swap the underscores (`_`) with periods (`.`). Below are some examples of names in the period separated style. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} one two.df two.2.df three.four.five three.four.five.2.vec this.is.period.separated ``` ::: ### Camel case ![](/images/camelCase.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} Camel case has no symbols to separate words. Instead after the first word every word starts with an upper case. Below are some examples of names in Camel Case. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} one twoDf two2Df threeFourFive threeFourFive2Vec thisIsCamelCase ``` ::: There are exceptions when you will want to break your preferred naming style.
